source.text: Klebsiella was isolated in this urine, which was sensitive to Bactrim and she was discharged on p.o. Bactrim.
She was advised to use ibuprofen over-the-counter two to three tabs t.i.d.
She is to follow up with Dr. Y in 7-10 days.

discharge_condition_source.text: Her symptoms responded to IV antibiotics and she remained clinically stable.

diagnosis_explanation:
Your kidneys are important organs. They filter waste from your blood. Pyelonephritis is an infection in your kidneys. This infection may have happened because of a blockage. A tube called a Foley catheter was in place. This tube connects to a pouch for urine. Sometimes, mucus can block this tube. This blockage can cause the kidney infection.

You also have high blood pressure. This is called hypertension. Your blood pressure was higher than normal. This can affect your health. Your kidneys are not filtering waste as well as they should. This is called mild renal insufficiency. You also have a low red blood cell count. This is called anemia. Red blood cells carry oxygen to your body.
medication_rationale:
Bactrim by mouth:
This medicine fights a type of germ that caused your kidney infection. It helps your body heal. You may notice an upset stomach or a rash. These are usually mild. Call your doctor if you get a bad rash, have trouble breathing, or your skin peels.

Ibuprofen two to three tabs three times daily:
This medicine helps with pain and fever. It reduces swelling. You might feel stomach upset. Taking it with food can help. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain, black stools, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and have some discomfort.
- Rest often but try to walk short distances inside.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Drink plenty of fluids to help flush your system.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your home daily.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a bit more energy.
- Continue to take short walks inside your home.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Drink plenty of fluids.
- Call your doctor if you notice cloudy or foul-smelling urine.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more comfortable and have more energy.
- You can gradually increase your walking time.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Keep drinking plenty of fluids.
- Call your doctor if you have pain when you urinate.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes, three times a day.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel much better and have good energy levels.
- You can resume most normal light activities.
- Avoid lifting anything heavier than 5 pounds for now.
- Keep drinking plenty of fluids.
- Call your doctor if you have back pain or a fever.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 20 minutes daily.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel significantly better over the next few weeks.
- Continue to stay hydrated.
- Follow up with your doctor as scheduled.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- You cannot keep fluids down: You can get dehydrated fast.
- Severe pain not helped by medicine: Your pain needs expert care.
- Leg swelling with pain: This could be a blood clot.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks mean the problem spreads.
- You feel very confused: This is a new problem.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that slowly gets better: This is normal healing.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can help you know.
- Mild redness of wound not spreading: This can happen while healing.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while you heal.
- You feel tired but improving: Your body is getting better.
